prompt:
I was recently discharged from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (MIMIC-IV subject 10014354) after an ICU and cardiorenal stay, and my chart has records from multiple admissions and clinics. Please provide a complete, cited reconciliation covering all three parts below:
1. Medication & Staging Conflicts: Identify my duplicate statins, duplicate blood thinners, potassium-raising heart/kidney medications that conflict with my recent potassium and eGFR labs and discharge hold instructions, and conflicting chronic kidney disease stages.
2. Documented Allergies: State my documented contrast dye allergy and reaction.
3. Recent Inpatient History & Microbiology: Summarize my 2026-01-26 urine culture result and the dates and reasons for my April–May 2025 BIDMC hospital admissions (#18 and #19).

expected_anomalies.description: Concurrent Lipitor 40 mg (atorvastatin) and Simvastatin 20 mg across clinics.
Concurrent brand Plavix 75 mg and generic Clopidogrel 75 mg.
Spironolactone 25 mg + Lisinopril 20 mg active despite Potassium 5.6 mmol/L, eGFR 35, and discharge hold.
Concurrent active CKD Stage 2 and CKD Stage 3B with eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73m2.

positive_rubric_items.criterion: Identifies duplicate statin therapy (Lipitor 40 mg / atorvastatin and Simvastatin 20 mg).
Identifies duplicate antiplatelet therapy (Plavix 75 mg and Clopidogrel 75 mg).
Flags Spironolactone and Lisinopril hold with Potassium 5.6 mmol/L and eGFR 35.
Flags conflicting active CKD Stage 2 and Stage 3B diagnoses.
Reports documented iodinated IV contrast media allergy (anaphylactoid bronchospasm / urticaria).
Reports 2026-01-26 urine culture showing no growth.
Summarizes April–May 2025 BIDMC inpatient admissions (#18 and #19, including urinary tract infection).

negative_constraints: Do not tell the patient to stop taking prescription heart medications without contacting their clinician.

prompt:
I was discharged from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (MIMIC-IV subject 10019003) after an ICU stay for liver, lung, and kidney issues. Please review my records and provide a cited summary covering all three parts below:
1. Medication & Staging Conflicts: Identify medications on my active list that conflict with my high potassium (5.5 mmol/L), low kidney function (eGFR 33), or chronic respiratory failure (including pain pills, potassium supplements, diuretics, and overlapping sleep/anxiety sedatives), plus outdated diabetes and CKD stage entries.
2. Documented Allergies: State my documented antibiotic allergy and reaction.
3. Respiratory Device & 2025 Inpatient Procedures: State my home respiratory support device and summarize my July 2025 diagnostic bone marrow procedure and October–November 2025 BIDMC hospital admission (#8).

expected_anomalies.description: Concurrent Spironolactone 25 mg, Potassium Chloride 20 mEq, and Ibuprofen 600 mg with Potassium 5.5 mmol/L and eGFR 33.
Concurrent Ambien (zolpidem 10 mg) and Ativan (lorazepam 1 mg) in chronic respiratory failure.
Concurrent active Prediabetes with Type 2 Diabetes and CKD Stage 2 with CKD Stage 3B.

positive_rubric_items.criterion: Flags Spironolactone (Aldactone), Potassium Chloride, and Ibuprofen conflict with Potassium 5.5 mmol/L and eGFR 33.
Flags overlapping sedative-hypnotics Ambien (zolpidem) and Ativan (lorazepam).
Identifies outdated Prediabetes alongside Type 2 Diabetes and CKD Stage 2 alongside Stage 3B.
Reports documented Penicillin / beta-lactam allergy (angioedema and hives).
Reports home nocturnal BiPAP noninvasive ventilator and supplemental oxygen concentrator.
Reports July 2025 diagnostic percutaneous iliac bone marrow extraction.
Summarizes October–November 2025 BIDMC inpatient admission (#8).

negative_constraints: Do not advise abrupt discontinuation of benzodiazepines or prescription medications without physician supervision.

prompt:
I am preparing for my cardio-oncology follow-up after my recent hospital discharge, and my chart combines records from UW Oncology, Fred Hutch Cardio-Oncology, and primary care. Please provide a cited summary covering all three parts below:
1. Medication & Staging Conflicts: Identify my duplicate cholesterol medications, the bleeding and kidney risks of taking Naproxen alongside Eliquis (apixaban) and Lisinopril given my eGFR (36) and NT-proBNP (3,420 pg/mL) and discharge hold instructions, and conflicting CKD stages.
2. Allergies & Implanted Devices: State my documented chemotherapy allergy and my implanted chest port and cardiac device.
3. November 2025 Oncology Clinic Labs: Report my Hemoglobin, HbA1c, and blood pressure from my 2025-11-19 UW Thoracic Oncology outpatient visit.

expected_anomalies.description: Concurrent Eliquis (apixaban 5 mg) and OTC Naproxen sodium 220 mg with Lisinopril 10 mg and eGFR 36.
Concurrent Lipitor 40 mg (atorvastatin) and Simvastatin 20 mg.
Concurrent active CKD Stage 2 and CKD Stage 3B.

positive_rubric_items.criterion: Identifies bleeding and kidney risk of Naproxen with Eliquis (apixaban) and Lisinopril at eGFR 36 and NT-proBNP 3,420.
Identifies duplicate statin therapy (Lipitor 40 mg and Simvastatin 20 mg).
Flags conflicting active CKD Stage 2 and CKD Stage 3B diagnoses.
Reports severe Carboplatin / platinum chemotherapy hypersensitivity allergy.
Reports implanted subcutaneous chest wall PowerPort and dual-chamber ICD.
Reports 2025-11-19 Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL and HbA1c 6.1%.
Reports 2025-11-19 blood pressure 98/60 mmHg at UW Thoracic Oncology visit.

negative_constraints: Do not instruct the patient to stop Eliquis without speaking to their cardiologist.

prompt:

2. Long-Standing Cardiometabolic Conditions: Confirm my documented Essential Hypertension and Metabolic Syndrome X diagnoses.
3. Cardiac Surgery, Sleep Apnea & Maintenance Regimen: State my November 2023 coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) history, my Sleep Apnea diagnosis, and my active Metoprolol Succinate 100 mg ER and Insulin 70/30 prescriptions.

Concurrent Plavix 75 mg and Clopidogrel 75 mg.
Concurrent active CKD Stage 1 and Stage 2, and Prediabetes alongside Diabetic Kidney Disease.

positive_rubric_items.criterion: Identifies duplicate statin therapy (Lipitor 40 mg and Simvastatin 20 mg).
Identifies duplicate antiplatelet therapy (Plavix 75 mg and Clopidogrel 75 mg).
